angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 178,099 km at 111.54 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.9652 +/- 0.0290 mas (same row, RUWE 1.23): 111.54 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.256 +/- 0.049 solar radii from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-88 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract): 178,099 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.258 +/- 0.066 solar masses from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-88 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3537 +/- 93 K from Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-88 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Crossfield et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-88 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJS..226....7C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-88.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.033, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
